content.text:
Replace the manual printer setup in JusPrin with the canvas's three-step "Add a printer" popup. Repo: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin. Work in your own new worktree off jusprin-newui. FIRST check feasibility and report to Kenneth; build only after he agrees.

## Today's behaviour (verified in code 2026-10-20)
In the printer chat, the header button "Browse the full printer list" (AgentUI/src/App.tsx ~611, and the error fallback in PrinterSetup/PrinterPanel.cpp ~108) sends `manual_setup` to the host. PrinterConversation.cpp ~658 calls OrcaPrinterBackend::run_manual_setup(), which runs `wxGetApp().run_wizard(ConfigWizard::RR_USER, ConfigWizard::SP_PRINTERS)`. In GUI_App::run_wizard (upstream OrcaSlicer code) that opens GuideFrame at BBL_MODELS_ONLY: OrcaSlicer's own printer-model selection page. The printers added there are saved under their own names (Printers::name_installed_printers), and the conversation gets the note "The person added … from OrcaSlicer's printer list." The button reads "Open printer settings" once a printer is picked.

## The design (source of truth: the Claude canvas artifact; Figma is retired)
Canvas "JusPrin v2", https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, page "Printer & Material Settings". Read these with the Artifact tool (action "read", path "project/<file>"):
- printer-prepare-first-print-light-add-printer-step-1.dc.html (and -dark-): "STEP 1 OF 3 · Which printer?". Brand select (Creality), Model select (Ender 3 V2), Nozzle segmented control (0.25 / 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8). "FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK" with a row "Bambu Lab P1S · 01P00A3B" and a status dot. "you can connect it later".
- ...-add-printer-step-2: "Which plate is on it?": Textured PEI ("ships with the MK4"), Smooth PEI, Satin.
- ...-add-printer-step-3: "What spool is on it right now?". "Search brand or material". "Common on the MK4": Prusament PLA, eSun PLA+, Polymaker PolyTerra PLA. "Nothing yet — I'll pick it later".
- Also onboarding-10a-choose-printer-setup-path-light.dc.html ("Configure manually: Choose the printer model, nozzle, plate, and material yourself.").
The Design System artifact, https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL, has the components (Select, SegmentedControl, FieldSearch, Menu rows, Sheet).

## Feasibility to check first (report findings with file:line evidence, then ask Kenneth)
1. Network discovery. Can step 1's "Found on your network" list come from code that exists today? Look at PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.*, OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection, the Bambu network agent (and the in-process fake in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md), and OrcaSlicer's own device discovery (SSDP/mDNS, Moonraker, PrusaLink). Which printer kinds can be found, and can picking a found printer both choose its preset (model, nozzle) and link the saved printer to that physical device in the same step? What can only happen later through "connect"? Attribute each behaviour to upstream OrcaSlicer or the JusPrin fork (AGENTS.md "Upstream vs. fork attribution").
2. Plate (step 2). In OrcaSlicer the bed type is a plate/project setting (curr_bed_type; PlateSettingsDialog), with per-printer defaults and compatibility. Can "the plate on this printer" be stored with the saved printer so new projects start with it, without a fork-owned settings change? If not, say what the closest OrcaSlicer concept is.
3. Spool (step 3). Kenneth decided on 2026-09-26 that there is no saved-spool concept: no remembered reels per printer, no colour words. Use only what OrcaSlicer keeps: installed filament presets, project filament slots with one colour each, per-printer memory of the last slots and colours, device trays, and sync from trays on request. Work out what step 3 can honestly mean under those rules: probably "pick the filament preset to start with", or tray sync for a connected Bambu printer. Propose the wording change ("spool" is a word the app doesn't hold). Check whether "Common on the MK4" has a real data source (vendor profiles' recommended filaments?) or would be invented.
4. Brand/model/nozzle lists. Confirm they can come from the installed vendor profiles (PrinterCatalog.*), including vendors not yet installed, and what installing a vendor costs (ConfigWizard does that today).
5. Anything in the design that OrcaSlicer cannot do, and the closest thing it can.

## When building (after Kenneth agrees)
- The popup replaces run_wizard for the manual path. Keep the outcome contract: the saved printer gets its own name, PrinterConversation posts the "added" note and starts a turn, and closing without finishing changes nothing.
- Read agent-docs/jusprin/README.md, design-system.md ("Writing UI code"; tokens only) and fork-stewardship.md before touching files outside src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/.
- Fail-first for every new guard test (restore from a saved copy, never `git checkout`). Test with the printer UI testing setup (Testing/README.md, isolated --datadir; never drive another JusPrin instance, Kenneth may have one open).
- Capture each step in light and dark, and send Kenneth the pictures.
- No live AI model calls without Kenneth's approval. Commit only when he asks.

=== never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
---
name: never-reuse-another-sessions-worktree
description: "A clean, merged, idle worktree under .claude/worktrees still belongs to its session; its owner can resume and check out over you mid-run. Always create your own."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: cb4c8804-b0a0-4ca0-b4a5-6b6998947d4b
  modified: 2026-09-24T00:36:34.672Z
---

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. An hour later its owning session resumed, checked out two other branches there (the reflog shows it), rewrote ~13,800 resource files, and my running harness crashed with "Could not load bitmap: bed_high_templ" -- a symptom that looked like a product bug.

**Why:** "clean and idle" says nothing about ownership. The session that created a worktree can resume at any time, and it has no way to know someone else moved in.

**How to apply:** create a new worktree with its own name (`git worktree add -b <branch> .claude/worktrees/<name> <base>`) and configure a fresh build dir with the flags in [[jusprin-worktree-build]]. At jusprin-newui bd8ea51abc a fresh build of `jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs agent_bridge_tests shell_integration_harness` was 881 ninja steps, not the hour I feared. If a harness run dies strangely, check `git -C <worktree> reflog -3 --date=iso` and file mtimes before suspecting the code. Related: [[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]].
=== jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).
=== add-printer-flow-figma-discrepancy
---
name: add-printer-flow-figma-discrepancy
description: "Add Printer Flow verified against Figma (2026-09-13): 18f matches closely, but 'Set it up myself' opens the stock Orca ConfigWizard, not the Figma-designed 18e grid"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

Verified the JusPrin v2 Figma file's "Add Printer Flow" page
(https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2, frames
18a-18f) against the running app on 2026-09-13, on the
figma-design-file-42aa00 worktree rebased onto
claude/add-printer-flow-changes-d2e0fa (commit cb5fe93e05 "Apply the Add
Printer Flow Figma changes to the dialog").

**Matches well:** 18f "No agent connected" state — text, layout, icon,
button, and the "Or **set it up myself** from the lists" footer are a close
match to Figma. "Set up the agent" correctly routes to the Agent Setup
empty-state page per Figma's cross-page note.

**Confirmed discrepancy:** the "set it up myself" link does NOT open the
Figma-designed 18e screen (a scoped grid of just Bambu Lab models, with a
Printer/Filaments/Bed shape/Firmware sidebar and an "Ask the agent instead"
link, inside the same "Add a printer" modal chrome). Instead it opens Orca's
stock `ConfigWizard` "Printer Selection" page — the same generic
all-vendors grid (Klipper, Marlin, RepRap, Afinia, ...) shown in the
first-run Setup Wizard, with plain Confirm/Create/Cancel buttons and no
scoping or "Ask the agent instead" link. Confirmed both by code
(`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:338`/`:401` calls Orca's own `ConfigWizard`) and by
driving the real app.

**Not independently visually verified this pass:** 18a (Initial evidence
entry), 18b (Recognized), 18c (Network Selected), 18d (Ambiguous) — these
need either a live configured OpenAI agent or a real discovered network
printer, neither available in the sandboxed test environment. Code
(`PrinterSetupDialog.cpp:471,702`) has these states named to match the Figma
frame numbers, suggesting intentional alignment, but this wasn't visually
confirmed. `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp --printer-setup` (via
`open_printer_setup_with` fixtures) is the deterministic way to reach these
states without live network/API dependencies — worth using for full
coverage.

**How to reproduce the live check:** ditto the built `.app`, replace
`CFBundleIdentifier`, ad-hoc codesign, launch with a scratch
`--datadir` and no `OPENAI_API_KEY` (lands cleanly on 18f without live
network calls). See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] for the general recipe.
computer-use's `request_access` was denied on the first attempt (likely an
unattended auto-deny) and granted on retry — don't assume denial is final,
but don't hammer retries either; ask the user first.

Related: [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]], [[figma-jusprin-v2-file]].
=== filament-chip-no-spool-decisions
---
name: filament-chip-no-spool-decisions
description: Kenneth's decisions for the Prepare header printer and filament chip - no saved spools, OrcaSlicer concepts only, no colour words, sync on request.
metadata:
  type: project
---

Decided by Kenneth on 2026-09-26 for the printer and filament chip in the Prepare header.

- The saved-spool concept (filament + colour + name, remembered per printer) is removed. The chip and its menus use only what OrcaSlicer already keeps: installed filaments, project filament slots with one colour each, per-printer memory of the last slots and colours, saved custom colours, device trays, and the sync from trays.
- No colour words anywhere in the UI (hover text, menus, chat line). Colour is shown as a swatch only.
- Copying the printer's trays into the project happens on request only, never automatically.
- Design lives in the claude.ai/design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", file `Orca Prepare Wireframes.dc.html`, turn 23 (marked proposed, supersedes turn 15's spool rules).

**Why:** Kenneth found the spool concept overcomplicated. Colour words are out because colour is stored as a hex value only; a word would be data the app does not hold. Automatic sync would overwrite a saved multi-colour project's slots.

**How to apply:** Do not propose names for reels, remembered spool lists, or colour names derived from hex values. When a design or code question touches filament selection, start from the OrcaSlicer concept that already stores the fact. Related: [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]], [[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]].

=== fake-bambu-printer-sim
---
name: fake-bambu-printer-sim
description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b5985db0-8e89-40a4-b560-5b7dcd439f2d
  modified: 2026-09-16T15:54:40.830Z
---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. === jusprin-chip-orca-seams
---
name: jusprin-chip-orca-seams
description: How the printer/spool chip reaches Orca without driving hidden controls — the four setup entry points and the two that are non-obvious.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.{hpp,cpp}` is the single place fork
code changes Orca's machine/material setup (added 2026-09-06, branch
`claude/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256`). The two seams that took real
digging:

- **Bed type.** `Plater::priv::on_select_bed_type` is private and reads the
  sidebar combo. But `Sidebar::set_bed_type_accord_combox(BedType)` is **public**
  and calls `ComboBox::SelectAndNotify`, which fires Orca's own handler — so the
  app-config write, the invalidation of plates on the default bed, and the
  re-render all stay upstream. Orca itself calls it from `Sidebar::update_presets`.
  `get_cur_combox_bed_types()` gives the per-model filtered list. This is reuse,
  not simulated input; do not reimplement the apply sequence.
- **Filament preset for extruder 0.** No public single call exists — the only
  entry point is a `wxEVT_COMBOBOX` carrying a `PlaterPresetComboBox` as event
  object, and firing that *would* be driving a hidden control. Compose the public
  parts instead: `set_filament_preset(0,…)` → `update_project_dirty_from_presets`
  → `export_selections` → `on_filament_change(0)` → `Tab::select_preset` →
  `on_config_change`.

Printer preset goes through the public
`Plater::update_objects_position_when_select_preset(...)` wrapper (keeps objects
on plates when bed shape changes). Colour follows
`PlaterPresetComboBox::sync_colour_config`. Preset import is one call:
`MainFrame::load_config_file()`.

Every path ends in `Plater::on_config_change`, whose last line publishes
`ProjectStateChangeReason::Settings` — which `StatusRow` already subscribes to,
so the chip and the pinned card refresh with no second path.

Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]].

On 2026-09-23 I reused `.claude/worktrees/compassionate-gould-f98259` to skip a full build: it was clean, detached at a commit already merged into jusprin-newui, no process had files open there, and its build dir was only 9 days old. === jusprin-worktree-build
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

=== jusprin-chip-orca-seams
---
name: jusprin-chip-orca-seams
description: How the printer/spool chip reaches Orca without driving hidden controls — the four setup entry points and the two that are non-obvious.
metadata:
  type: project
---

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.{hpp,cpp}` is the single place fork
code changes Orca's machine/material setup (added 2026-09-06, branch
`claude/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256`). The two seams that took real
digging:

- **Bed type.** `Plater::priv::on_select_bed_type` is private and reads the
  sidebar combo. But `Sidebar::set_bed_type_accord_combox(BedType)` is **public**
  and calls `ComboBox::SelectAndNotify`, which fires Orca's own handler — so the
  app-config write, the invalidation of plates on the default bed, and the
  re-render all stay upstream. Orca itself calls it from `Sidebar::update_presets`.
  `get_cur_combox_bed_types()` gives the per-model filtered list. This is reuse,
  not simulated input; do not reimplement the apply sequence.
- **Filament preset for extruder 0.** No public single call exists — the only
  entry point is a `wxEVT_COMBOBOX` carrying a `PlaterPresetComboBox` as event
  object, and firing that *would* be driving a hidden control. Compose the public
  parts instead: `set_filament_preset(0,…)` → `update_project_dirty_from_presets`
  → `export_selections` → `on_filament_change(0)` → `Tab::select_preset` →
  `on_config_change`.

Printer preset goes through the public
`Plater::update_objects_position_when_select_preset(...)` wrapper (keeps objects
on plates when bed shape changes). Colour follows
`PlaterPresetComboBox::sync_colour_config`. Preset import is one call:
`MainFrame::load_config_file()`.

Every path ends in `Plater::on_config_change`, whose last line publishes
`ProjectStateChangeReason::Settings` — which `StatusRow` already subscribes to,
so the chip and the pinned card refresh with no second path.

Related: [[render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof]], [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]].

---
name: jusprin-claude-design-system-artifact
description: "The two Claude artifacts mirroring the Figma file JusPrin v2 (a Design System and a Design canvas): URLs, where the re-sync tools and backups live, how a re-sync is proven safe, what was measured on 2026-10-13, known gaps."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 18e047ce-4892-4a44-8b70-c447eb34727c
  modified: 2026-10-13T20:50:06.847Z
---

Two private artifacts in Kenneth's Claude account mirror the Figma file
([[figma-jusprin-v2-file]]). Since 2026-10-20 these artifacts ARE the source of truth ([[design-source-is-claude-artifacts]]); edit them directly. The Figma re-sync steps below are history.

1. Design System: https://claude.ai/artifact/3zgiix8rAw3rXextQnR5UL (version 9)
   - `tokens.json` + `tokens.css`, 37 coded React components (`window.JusPrin`).
   - Each component card: every variant Figma draws, a Light and a Dark panel,
     then the coded component. The page lists them as one flat table in bundle
     order with code names; it draws no group headings.
   - `screens/<page>/<screen>.spec.txt` (166) + `screens/index.json`: plain
     files for agents, one resolved line per layer.
2. Design canvas "JusPrin v2": https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v
   (version 7): 10 pages with Figma's names in Figma's order, 198 artboards at
   their Figma x,y and in Figma's layer order, each drawn in the Light or Dark
   mode Figma sets on it; "… · Light & Dark" review frames are drawn whole.

Tools, reads and backups are durable now, outside the repo:
`~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/figma-mirror/` — start with
its `README.md` (step-by-step re-sync). `published/` is an exact copy of what is
live; `backup-2026-10-13-before-reimport/` holds the earlier state with the
scripts that reproduce it byte for byte.

How Kenneth wants a re-sync done (2026-10-13): back up first, re-import, then
compare the backup with the new import so nothing already in sync regresses.
The method that worked, in order:
- rebuild from the old reads and require byte-identical output (proves the
  scripts);
- re-read Figma with the old script and diff the reads (proves Figma unchanged:
  all 14 files were identical);
- only then change scripts, and explain every file `compare_builds.py` reports;
- score every artboard against Figma's own page screenshots
  (`visual_compare.py`) and allow no artboard to score worse.
Result of that run: 0 artboards further from Figma, 36 closer; boards within 5
of Figma (0–255 scale) went from 99 to 122 of 186; all 37 cards and 163 of 166
spec files came out byte-identical; tokens matched Figma's variables exactly.

What the screenshot comparison caught that file checks could not: dark panels I
had added behind dark variants (Figma has none), frames forced dark by a "dark"
in their name (use Figma's `explicitVariableModes` instead), a frame half light
and half dark through a nested mode, sets whose background is a two-stop linear
gradient, Figma's GRID layout (children need their own positions), and small
frames centred in the 40px-minimum artboard instead of top-left.

Other traps: an absolutely positioned layer followed by in-flow siblings paints
over them in HTML (give the later siblings `position:relative`); Figma tints
icons with a mask plus a coloured rectangle; the Artifact tool's bulk read
prints small text files into context, so have a background agent do large
backups; a session scratchpad is wiped on restart — never keep the only copy of
tools there; when two reads of a page exist, keep the later one by timestamp.

Known gaps: photographs and 3D renders are flat placeholders (the 16 worst
scores are all such screens); radial and image fills are placeholders; Figma
stacks 12 dark screens on top of light ones on "Printer & Material Settings"
and the canvas keeps that; ProjectCard and PrinterCard variants are stacked in
Figma and laid out in a row on the canvas; "Add Printer Flow (Obsolete)" is not
read; Notice/Strip drifts a few px vertically.

Figma vs code differences Kenneth has not ruled on (the artifacts hold Figma's):
dark status colours (Figma #4CAF82 / #E07080 / #E8B84A, code #58B894 / #F07A8E /
#E9B960), `radius/full` 10 vs `pill` 9999, Button/Icon 32px vs 26px, Menu/Row
36px full-width hover vs the app's 32px inset rows
([[header-menu-values-kenneth-kept]]). See also [[figma-mcp-view-seat-limit]]
and [[claude-in-chrome-lives-in-claude-profile]].

Direct editing (2026-10-20): work on a copy of the live files (`figma-mirror/live-<date>` -> `work/`),
publish only the changed files, then rsync `work/` into `published/`. The canvas holds its own copy of the
design system in `project/ds/jusprin/` (tokens.css/json, components/bundle.*) — change both artifacts
together. `tools/composer/render.py` screenshots boards with headless Chrome (no type runtime needed);
measure natural board heights in the built-in browser and fix both the board file and canvas.json
(`resize_board.py`). `index.d.ts` must be published with contentType text/plain. The DS card height lives
in the `@dsCard height=` comment. Added then: `surface-raised-hover` (menu-row highlight, dark #3B3047) and
`component-composer-maxLines` (8); the new Composer is drawn by `tools/composer/composer_html.py`.

input.prompt:
You are doing READ-ONLY code research in the JusPrin repository (a fork of OrcaSlicer, C++/wxWidgets). Worktree: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/add-printer-popup (branch off `jusprin-newui`). Always use absolute paths or `cd <worktree> &&` in every Bash command (the shell cwd resets). Do not edit any file, do not build, do not run the app.

Context: we plan a 3-step "Add a printer" popup. Step 1 picks Brand / Model / Nozzle from lists, and also shows a "FOUND ON YOUR NETWORK" list of printers (example row: "Bambu Lab P1S · 01P00A3B" with a green status dot) with the note "you can connect it later". Question: can that list come from code that exists today, and what does picking a found printer give us?

Answer these, each with file:line evidence:
1. What does `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp` `discover_printers()` actually return — which device kinds? It reads `DeviceManager::get_my_machine_list()`. Find out in `src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceCore/DevManager.*` what that list contains: LAN-discovered Bambu printers (SSDP via the Bambu network plug-in `on_ssdp_msg`), cloud-bound printers (needs Bambu sign-in), or both? Is discovery running when the app has not selected a Bambu printer profile? Look at `NetworkAgent::start_discovery`, `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent`, and `OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:237) — does SSDP discovery need the Bambu network plug-in to be installed/loaded? Does it need a BBL printer preset selected or the Bambu printer agent installed? What happens on a machine where the plug-in is not installed?
2. For a found Bambu device, what does `MachineObject` give: `printer_type` (device model id like "C12"/"N1"), `get_dev_name()`, dev id (serial), IP, nozzle diameter (only after connecting? or in the SSDP message?). Can the device model id be mapped to a catalog model? See `PrinterCatalog::find_device_model` in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterCatalog.cpp and `model_id` in resources/profiles/BBL/machine/*.json. Is the nozzle diameter known before a connection (access code) is made?
3. Non-Bambu discovery in OrcaSlicer: is there any mDNS/Bonjour browsing (src/slic3r/Utils/Bonjour.*, src/slic3r/GUI/BonjourDialog.*, the "Browse" button in PhysicalPrinterDialog) for OctoPrint/Moonraker/PrusaLink? Is it triggered only on demand from that dialog? What service types does it browse (e.g. _octoprint._tcp)? Does it find Moonraker/Klipper or PrusaLink printers, and does it report a printer model or just a host name/address? Also check Elegoo/Creality/Flashforge/other vendor-specific discovery in src/slic3r/Utils (e.g. ElegooLink, Flashforge, CrealityPrint, SimplyPrint) — anything that enumerates devices on the LAN.
4. Linking: `OrcaPrinterBackend::add_printer` takes `AddPrinterRequest.device_id` and passes it to `Printers::add_named_printer` (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Printers/NamedPrinters.*). Does saving with a device_id link the saved printer to that physical device at once? What does `connect_printer` (OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:391) add on top (access code for LAN mode, `set_selected_machine`, verification)? So: in one step, can picking a found Bambu printer both choose the preset (model from printer_type; nozzle?) and record the device link, leaving only access code / verification for "connect later"? Check how the existing printer chat's `printer_add` tool uses device_id (grep in src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp and the AgentUI tool definitions under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src for printer tools).
5. The in-process fake Bambu printer: read src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md and FakeBambuAgent.*. Does the fake show up in `get_my_machine_list()` / `discover_printers()` without connecting, so it could be used to test a "found on your network" row?

Attribution (required): for each behaviour you report, say whether upstream OrcaSlicer ships it or the JusPrin fork added it. Method: the upstream merge base is commit 3ffb9585d2. Check `git -C <worktree> show 3ffb9585d2:<path> | grep -n <symbol>` — present there means upstream; anything under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/ is fork. For a fork seam in an upstream file, `git -C <worktree> log -L` or `git blame` the line. If you did not check, say "unverified".

Report: concise, plain English, one short section per question, each claim with file:line. Label anything you inferred rather than read as "inference". End with a 5-line summary: which printer kinds can appear in the list, what picking one can set immediately, what must wait for "connect".

<result>Short answer: yes, the plate can be stored with a saved printer using only settings OrcaSlicer already has, and new projects pick it up, but there are three catches. The value has to be written as a number. A plate the person picks later in the sidebar takes over from it. And for most non-Bambu printers, including the MK4 and Ender-3 V2, Orca never shows the plate.

Everything below is upstream OrcaSlicer unless marked fork. I checked each upstream claim against 3ffb9585d2. I read code only; nothing was run.

## 1. Where Orca keeps the bed type
- **The enum** has six real plates plus "Default" (`PrintConfig.hpp:314-322`). The stored names are at `PrintConfig.cpp:469-477`.
- **Display labels** come from `PrintConfig.cpp:1092-1097`: "Smooth Cool Plate", "Engineering Plate", "Smooth High Temp Plate", "Textured PEI Plate", "Textured Cool Plate" and "Cool Plate (SuperTack)".
  - There is no "Satin" and no "Smooth PEI". The closest to Smooth PEI is "High Temp Plate", shown as "Smooth High Temp Plate".
- **`curr_bed_type` belongs to the project**, not to the printer preset (project options list, `PresetBundle.cpp:53`). So it cannot be saved into a printer preset.
- **Saving:** each plate's own value goes into the 3MF as `bed_type` metadata (`bbs_3mf.cpp:7921-7924`). The global value lives in `project_config`. I believe it lands in `Metadata/project_settings.config` (`bbs_3mf.cpp:210`), but that is inference.
- **Per-plate override:** a plate falls back to the global value when it has none of its own (`PartPlate.cpp:188-204`). The per-plate choice in PlateSettingsDialog is disabled for every non-Bambu printer (`PlateSettingsDialog.cpp:408-409`).

## 2. `default_bed_type`
- **It is a printer-preset option.** It is defined at `PrintConfig.cpp:1100-1106` with the comment "won't be shown in the UI", and it is in the printer options list (`Preset.cpp:1384`). It is absent from `Tab.cpp`, so the Printer settings tab does not show it, but a user preset will save it.
- **In printer-model files it does nothing in Orca's C++.** The code that reads model files (`PresetBundle.cpp:~4700-4810`) has no key for it. About 40 model files carry it anyway (Creality K-series, all Bambu models, Flashforge AD5M and others).
- **Text values don't work; I'm treating this as an upstream bug.** `Preset::get_default_bed_type` (`Preset.cpp:966-994`) runs `atoi` on the value:
  - `"4"` gives Textured PEI, as intended.
  - `"Textured PEI Plate"` reads as 0, logs an error and falls back to High Temp Plate, even though the option's own description says text is supported.
  - With no value at all, it returns Cool Plate for model IDs BL-P001, BL-P002 and C13, and High Temp Plate for everything else.

## 3. What happens when a printer is selected (`Sidebar::update_presets`, `Plater.cpp:2513-2545`)
1. **Bambu printers, or presets with `support_multi_bed_types` on:** the plate list is rebuilt. Orca then reads `app_config printer_settings[<preset name>]["curr_bed_type"]`. If that memory exists it wins; if not, `get_default_bed_type()` decides.
2. **Every other printer:** `get_default_bed_type()` is applied, and the plate dropdown is disabled and hidden (`:2537-2545`). The value still matters, because it decides which filament bed-temperature setting the slice uses (`Tab.cpp:4320-4338`). The compatibility check that warns when a filament's bed temperature for the chosen plate is 0 only runs for case 1 (`Print.cpp:1755`).
3. **Orca also remembers the last plate per preset name** in its app config, not in the preset file. It is written whenever the plate changes (`Plater.cpp:9478-9480`) and on export (`PresetBundle.cpp:2938`).

**Answering your question 3 directly:** a user printer preset saved with `default_bed_type: "2"` (or any number from 1 to 6) would start on that plate when selected, as long as there is no remembered value for that preset name. A brand-new preset name has none. Once the person picks a plate in the sidebar, the memory overrides the preset from then on.

New projects should pick this up too. `new_project` calls `reset()`, then `load_current_presets` (`Plater.cpp:12057+`), which I expect re-runs `update_presets`. That last step is inference; I didn't trace it to the end.

## 4. Which printers show a plate choice at all
- **The dropdown appears only for Bambu printers, or when `support_multi_bed_types` is on** (`Plater.cpp:647, 2545`). That option is visible in the Printer tab (`Tab.cpp:4487`), and about 140 vendor files set it to 1.
- **The Prusa MK4 and Ender-3 V2 profiles don't set it** (`Prusa MK4.json`, `Creality Ender-3 V2.json`, `fdm_creality_common.json`), so neither shows a plate.
- **Plates offered per printer:** the full list minus the model file's `not_support_bed_type` (`Plater.cpp:2794-2840`). For example, the Bambu P2S and H2D drop both Cool plates.

## 5. "Ships with the MK4"
No profile supports this. The Prusa MK4 and Ender-3 V2 model files have no `default_bed_type`, so the annotation would have to come from our own data.

## 6. Fork code (all under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`)
- **`PrinterCatalog.cpp:139, 164`** reads the model file's `default_bed_type` text, a field Orca itself ignores.
- **`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:86-93`** (it is in `PrinterSetup/`, not `Shell/`) shows the preset's `default_bed_type` text directly. This can disagree with what Orca actually picks. For example, the X1 Carbon file says "Textured PEI Plate" while Orca chooses Cool Plate (my inference from the code above).
- **`SetupCommands.cpp:511-526`** `select_bed_type` goes through `set_bed_type_accord_combox`, so Orca handles the project write and the per-preset memory itself.
- **`Printers/`** has no plate handling.

## Verdict
- **Can the plate be saved with the printer without a new setting?** Yes. Write a number into the user printer preset's existing `default_bed_type`; never text.
- **Will new projects start on it?** Yes, until the person picks another plate in the sidebar. After that, Orca's remembered value for that preset name wins. That memory sits in Orca's app config, so it isn't stored with the printer. I expect renaming the printer to lose it (inference).
- **Which printers it works for:** visibly, only Bambu printers and presets with `support_multi_bed_types` on. On the MK4 or Ender-3 V2 the value would silently set bed temperatures, but no plate is shown anywhere, and asking "which plate?" maps to nothing the person can see. Turning on `support_multi_bed_types` in the user preset is the existing way to show the dropdown on those printers.
- **What can't be offered:** "Satin" doesn't exist, and "Smooth PEI" is only "Smooth High Temp Plate".
- **Honest fallback:** ask step 2 only when Orca offers a plate choice, list only Orca's plates (minus that model's exclusions), and skip the step for every other printer.</result>

<result>I answered all six questions from the code and the shipped profiles; nothing was edited or run. The main finding: the mockup's three rows don't come from any data in the app, and for the MK4 two of them can't appear in any MK4-specific list. No Prusament profile is compatible with the MK4 at all.

**1. Is there real per-model data?**

There are two upstream fields.

- **`default_materials`** is on the model file (`Prusa MK4.json:11`, `Creality Ender-3 V2.json:11`, `Bambu Lab P1S.json:12`). It is parsed at `src/libslic3r/Preset.cpp:369-378`. Orca's setup wizard uses it to tick filaments when you pick a model (`WebGuideDialog.cpp:446-486`). The old `ConfigWizard.cpp:2137-2160` path does the same, but `run_wizard` now opens the web wizard (`GUI_App.cpp:8975-8979`). `load_installed_filaments` also installs these when a printer has no compatible filament installed (`PresetBundle.cpp:2552-2588`). All of this is upstream.
- **`default_filament_profile`** is on the nozzle profile and is a single entry. Examples: `Prusa MK4 0.4 nozzle.json:10-12`, `Creality Ender-3 V2 0.4 nozzle.json:9-11`, and for the P1S it is inherited from `fdm_bbl_3dp_001_common.json:21-23`.
- **Compatibility** comes from `is_compatible_with_printer` (`Preset.cpp:809-841`, upstream). The sidebar list shows filaments that are both installed (`is_visible`) and compatible. The fork's chip uses the same two flags (`SetupCommands.cpp:200-220`).
- **Compatible counts at 0.4 mm** (my own script over the profile files):
  - MK4: 10 Prusa presets.
  - Ender-3 V2: 6 Creality presets.
  - P1S: 219 BBL presets.
  - Every printer also gets the 234 OrcaFilamentLibrary presets, which include eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA. Their `compatible_printers` is empty, so they fit any printer unless a vendor ships a preset with the same name (`Preset.cpp:3704-3725`, `819-823`).
- **Prusament** profiles exist only for the CORE One and XL; none lists the MK4.

**2. What the fork does with filaments**

- `PrinterCatalog.cpp:160-163` reads `default_filament_profile` after resolving the inheritance chain (`resolve_machine`, lines 50-63). It keeps one entry per nozzle size (lines 271-290).
- `install_and_select_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:439-516`) passes that one filament as both the "filaments to install" list and the preferred filament to `apply_vendor_config`.
  - With `overwrite=false` it adds the filament to the installed list without removing any (`PresetBundle.cpp:1248-1255`).
  - It then makes it the active slot-1 filament (lines 1281-1295) and saves the selections (line 1298).
  - So it installs and selects exactly one filament preset.
- `apply_vendor_config` is upstream (present at `3ffb9585d2:src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:1138`).

**3. Searching by brand or material**

- Every preset carries `filament_vendor` and `filament_type`.
  - Generic presets inherit `"Generic"` (for example `Prusa/filament/fdm_filament_common.json:96`).
  - Branded ones name the brand: `"eSUN"`, `"Polymaker"`, `"Bambu Lab"`.
- The fork already reads both fields: `SetupCommands.cpp:51-68` and the `FilamentInfo` struct at `SetupCommands.hpp:40-52`.
- Uninstalled presets can be listed without reading the resource files, with one limit.
  - Orca loads every vendor bundle in the user's system folder, installed filaments or not, and only marks the installed ones visible (`Preset.cpp:865-868`).
  - The filament library bundle is always copied there (`PresetUpdater.cpp:1078`), but other vendors only once they are enabled (inferred from `PresetBundle.cpp:2195-2235`).
  - So library filaments are always listable. Prusa's own presets are listable only after the Prusa bundle is enabled; before that they exist only in `resources/profiles`.
- Installing a filament means setting `filaments/<name>=true` in app config (`AppConfig.cpp:47`). Orca does this from the wizard's filament page; `apply_vendor_config` is the programmatic route.
- There is no fork filament catalog. What exists is `compatible_filaments()` (installed and compatible only), `open_filament_library()` which opens Orca's own Add/Remove page (`SetupCommands.cpp:556-562`), and the chip menu that uses both (`FilamentMenu.cpp:426-454`).

**4. Per-printer memory of slots and colours**

This is upstream.
- `export_selections` writes, per printer name, the slot-1 filament, `filament_01…`, `filament_colors`, colour types and more into app config's `orca_presets` (`PresetBundle.cpp:2934-2960`, `AppConfig.cpp:801-803`, `1018-1019`).
- It is read back at startup (`load_selections`, lines 2723-2800) and on every printer switch when the "Remember printer configuration" preference is on, which is the default (`Tab.cpp:6229-6233`, `AppConfig.cpp:436-437`).
- A printer with no saved colours gets `#26A69A` in every slot (`PresetBundle.cpp:2657`).

Traced, partly inferred: after adding a printer with filament X, `apply_vendor_config` saves the selections with X in slot 1. Switching back to that printer later restores X. A new project keeps whatever is currently selected (inferred).

Not verified: whether the memory carries over to the person's named copy that `Printers::add_named_printer` saves (`NamedPrinters.cpp:201`).

**5. Syncing from the printer's trays**

- Upstream `Sidebar::sync_ams_list` (`Plater.cpp:3501`) needs a connected, selected machine. Otherwise it shows a "not connected" warning (lines 3505-3515).
- The fork already wires this up:
  - `sync_from_printer` (`SetupCommands.cpp:565-588`) requires a named printer with a connected device.
  - `printer_trays()` (lines 287-307) reports whether trays are available.
  - The chip has a "Use what's loaded on the printer…" row (`FilamentMenu.cpp:327-342`).
  - The add-printer code reads trays live: Bambu trays at `PrinterDiscovery.cpp:24-60`, Moonraker multi-filament lanes at `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:113-116`. These are fork structs called `spools`, but they are only device reports, nothing saved.
- Inference: sync during add-printer is possible only after the connection step has succeeded, or for a printer the app has already discovered and that reports its trays. It is never possible for a printer added by model alone.

**6. Colour**

- Picking a preset applies its `default_filament_colour` if it has one, and otherwise leaves the slot's colour unchanged. That is upstream `PresetComboBox.cpp:252-253`, mirrored by the fork at `SetupCommands.cpp:330-332`.
- Nearly all shipped presets leave it empty: 788 of about 840 values are `""`. That includes Prusa Generic PLA @MK4, eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA.
- Colours are always hex values: the project's `filament_colour` and trays' `#RRGGBB`. The colour grid tooltip shows the hex key (`FilamentMenu.cpp:167`).
- A colour word would only be needed if the mockup labelled rows by colour. Nothing in the data supplies one.

**(a) Does "Common on the <model>" have a data source?**

There is no data on what is common. The closest real field is `default_materials`, the wizard's ticks:
- **MK4:** "Prusa Generic PLA-CF; Prusa Generic PC; Prusa Generic PVA; Prusa Generic PA; Prusa Generic PA-CF; Prusa Generic ABS @MK4; Prusa Generic PLA @MK4; Prusa Generic PETG @MK4; Prusa Generic TPU @MK4; Prusa Generic ASA @MK4". There is no Prusament, eSUN or Polymaker.
- **Ender-3 V2:** "Creality Generic PLA; Creality Generic PETG; Creality Generic ABS".
- **P1S:** "Bambu PLA Matte, Bambu PLA Basic, Bambu PLA-CF, Bambu PETG-CF, Bambu ABS, Bambu PLA Silk, Bambu PAHT-CF, Bambu Support For PLA, Bambu Support For PA/PET, Generic PLA, Generic PLA High Speed, Generic PETG, Bambu PETG HF". All the Bambu-branded entries end in "@BBL X1C".

eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA would only show up through a search of the filament library. Prusament PLA cannot show for the MK4 at all.

**(b) What step 3 can honestly do**

- Default to the profile's own default filament: Prusa Generic PLA @MK4, Creality Generic PLA, or Bambu PLA Basic @BBL X1C.
- List that model's `default_materials` under a heading like "Suggested for this printer".
- Search compatible presets by `filament_vendor` and `filament_type`, covering the library plus the vendor's own presets.
- Install the chosen one and put it in slot 1 through `install_and_select_printer`'s filament argument. Orca's per-printer memory then brings it back whenever this printer is selected.
- Offer "Use what's loaded" only if the connection step has succeeded and trays are reported.
- Never show a colour name, and leave the slot colour as it is unless the preset has a default colour.
- "Pick it later" can simply keep the profile default, which is what happens today.

**(c) Suggested wording, without "spool"**

- **Title:** "Which filament will you print with first?" or "Choose a filament for this printer".
- **Search field:** "Search brand or material".
- **List heading:** "Suggested for the MK4". This is honest because it is the profile's own list; "Common on" claims usage data the app doesn't have.
- **Link:** "Skip — use OrcaSlicer's default (Prusa Generic PLA)".</result>

content.text:
Here's the feasibility report: the agents' findings, checked by me against the code. I've spot-checked the key claims.

The popup can be built in the printer chat's React page, using printer-setup code that already exists. Brand, model, nozzle and saving the printer can come from current code with almost no new plumbing. Three parts of the design show things OrcaSlicer doesn't hold: printers of any brand found on the network, the "Satin" and "Smooth PEI" plates, and a "Common on the MK4" list of filament brands. Each section below says what we can actually show instead. Five decisions at the end need your answer before I build.

## 1. "Found on your network"

- **Only Bambu Lab printers can be found today.**
  - The fork's `discover_printers()` (`PrinterSetup/PrinterDiscovery.cpp:76-85`) reads OrcaSlicer's `DeviceManager::get_my_machine_list()` (`DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:651-675`, upstream).
  - That list holds Bambu printers bound to a signed-in Bambu account, plus LAN printers the app already has an access code for. A brand-new printer with no access code sits only in `get_local_machinelist()`. The fork's `connection()` reads that fuller list at `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:335-347`.
- **Bambu's LAN search has two preconditions**, both upstream:
  - It needs Bambu's network plug-in installed (`BBLPrinterAgent.cpp:104-113`).
  - It needs the Bambu printer agent active, which OrcaSlicer only picks when a Bambu printer profile is selected (`GUI_App.cpp:3572-3586`).
- **Other brands are only searched on demand.** OrcaSlicer's OctoPrint mDNS browse (`BonjourDialog.cpp:126`), the Creality K-series scan and the Flashforge broadcast all run only from the Browse button in the physical-printer dialog (`PhysicalPrinterDialog.cpp:212-256`, upstream). Moonraker has no discovery at all.
- **What picking a found printer can set at once:**
  - The model: the device reports a model id, for example C12 for the P1S, and the fork's catalogue maps it (`PrinterCatalog.cpp:137,182`).
  - The link between the saved printer and that device. `add_printer` already accepts a device id and records the link (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:177`, `Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp:184-206`, fork), but nothing passes one today (`PrinterConversation.cpp:503-506`).
- **What waits for "connect":**
  - The nozzle. It is unknown until the printer reports it after connecting (`DevNozzleSystem.h:18`, upstream). We'd assume 0.4, and the fork's existing nozzle-mismatch check flags it after connecting (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:383-387`).
  - The access code, selecting the machine, and verifying the connection.
- **The printer chat's Add opening already shows this same found-printer list** (`PrinterConversation.cpp:175-185`).
- **The fake Bambu printer connects itself instantly** (`Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp:521-547`). It can test a found row, but never the "found, not yet connected" state.

## 2. Plate

- **The plate belongs to the project, not the printer.** `curr_bed_type` is a project setting (`PresetBundle.cpp:53`, upstream).
- **OrcaSlicer remembers the last plate per printer name anyway.** When a printer is selected, it uses that memory first, and the printer profile's hidden `default_bed_type` otherwise (`Plater.cpp:2518-2531`, upstream).
  - Calling the fork's existing `select_bed_type` (`SetupCommands.cpp:511`) right after saving writes that memory, exactly as a plate pick in the sidebar does. No new setting is needed.
  - Inference: the memory is keyed by name, so it is probably lost if the printer is renamed.
- **Most non-Bambu printers have no plate choice.** OrcaSlicer shows the plate dropdown only for Bambu printers or profiles with `support_multi_bed_types` on (`Plater.cpp:2512, 2545`). The MK4 and Ender 3 V2 profiles have it off.
- **OrcaSlicer has six plates:** Smooth Cool, Engineering, Smooth High Temp, Textured PEI, Textured Cool and SuperTack (`PrintConfig.cpp:1092-1097`). There is no "Satin" and no "Smooth PEI".
- **"Ships with the MK4" has no source.** About 40 model files name a default plate, but the MK4's doesn't.

## 3. Filament ("spool")

- **"Common on the MK4" has no data behind it.**
  - The nearest real field is the model's `default_materials`, the list OrcaSlicer's setup wizard pre-ticks (upstream).
  - For the MK4 that is ten "Prusa Generic …" presets (`Prusa MK4.json:11`). There is no Prusament, eSUN or Polymaker.
  - Every Prusament profile lists only the CORE One as compatible (`Prusament PLA @CORE One.json:15`), so Prusament PLA can never appear for an MK4.
  - eSUN PLA+ and PolyTerra PLA exist only in OrcaSlicer's general filament library, which fits every printer.
- **What step 3 can honestly do:** pick one filament preset to start with.
  - The fork's `install_and_select_printer` already installs one filament preset and puts it in slot 1, through upstream `apply_vendor_config` (`SetupCommands.cpp:439-509`).
  - OrcaSlicer's per-printer memory of slots and colours then brings it back whenever this printer is selected (`PresetBundle.cpp:2934-2960`). Whether that memory carries over to the person's named copy is unverified.
- **Tray sync is impossible here.** It needs a connected printer (`Plater.cpp:3501-3515`), and a printer being added isn't connected yet.
- **No colour words are needed.** Most presets set no colour.

## 4. Brand, model, nozzle

- **The catalogue covers vendors the person hasn't installed.** The fork's catalogue reads every packaged vendor (`PrinterCatalog.cpp:98-106`): 64 brands, 383 models, 983 model-and-nozzle combinations.
- **Nozzle sizes vary per model, so the control has to show each model's own sizes.**
  - 181 models ship one size, and some ship up to eight.
  - The MK4 ships 0.25 / 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8; the Ender 3 V2 ships 0.4 only.
  - With one size, I'd hide the control.
- **Two brand spellings need folding.** The catalogue splits SecKit and Seckit into two brands, so I'd group by vendor file.
- **Installing is already written and safe.** `add_printer` adds the new model to the person's setup without removing anything, and rolls back on failure (upstream `PresetBundle.cpp:1264-1273`).
  - The first printer from a vendor copies that vendor's profiles into the data folder, about 4 MB for Creality, then reloads all presets. I haven't timed it.
- **Today's button opens OrcaSlicer's web setup guide**, not the old ConfigWizard (`GUI_App.cpp`, `run_wizard`, upstream).

## 5. Gaps in the design itself

- **No buttons.** None of the three boards draws Back, Next, Cancel or a close button, so nothing on step 1 moves forward.
- **Mismatched examples.** Step 1 shows an Ender 3 V2, steps 2 and 3 talk about the MK4, and the Ender 3 V2 only ships a 0.4 nozzle.
- **Different screen.** The boards draw the popup over the Prepare screen. In code, the manual path starts from the printer chat on Home. The popup would open over that chat.

## Decisions for you

**1. Should the network list show only Bambu printers the app has already found, without starting a search itself?**
- (a) Show what OrcaSlicer's device list already holds, including new printers that have no access code yet, and hide the section when it's empty. This has no side effects, but on a computer with a non-Bambu printer selected and no Bambu sign-in it will usually be empty.
- (b) Start Bambu's search when the popup opens. This finds more, but it swaps the network provider of the currently selected non-Bambu printer until its profile next changes, and it does nothing without Bambu's plug-in.
- (c) Drop the section. The printer chat's opening already lists found printers.

I recommend (a). Picking a row fills in brand and model and pre-selects 0.4. The saved printer is linked to that device, and connecting stays a separate step.

**2. Should step 2 only appear for printers where OrcaSlicer offers a plate choice?**
- (a) Show it only for Bambu printers and profiles with multiple plate types, using OrcaSlicer's own plate names. Other printers get a two-step popup. The choice is saved as OrcaSlicer's per-printer plate memory, the same as a sidebar pick.
- (b) Always ask, and turn on `support_multi_bed_types` in the saved printer so the sidebar shows the plate. This changes a printer setting the vendor left off.
- (c) Always ask, and store the answer where nothing shows it. People would make a choice they never see again.

I recommend (a).

**3. Should step 3 become "Which filament do you want to start with?"** Under it would sit a list headed "Suggested for the MK4", taken from the model's `default_materials`. A search would cover filaments compatible with that printer. The skip link would read "Skip — start with Prusa Generic PLA @MK4", the profile's own default.
- Yes, as worded.
- Yes, with your wording.
- Something else.

I recommend yes, as worded. It drops "spool" and the invented "Common on" list, and claims only what the profiles say.

**4. Should I add the missing Back, Next and Cancel controls in code first, or should the canvas boards be updated first?**
- (a) Code first. The controls would follow the printer chat's existing dialog buttons: Next on step 1, choosing a row in steps 2 and 3 moves on, Back returns, Cancel or Escape closes with nothing saved. I'd send you light and dark captures of each step and update the canvas after you approve.
- (b) Canvas first. This waits on a design pass before any code.

I recommend (a).

**5. When the printer chat page fails to load, should its native fallback button keep opening OrcaSlicer's printer list?**
- (a) Keep OrcaSlicer's printer list there (`PrinterPanel.cpp:108-113`). The React popup can't appear when the page itself failed, and this case is rare.
- (b) Build a second, native version of the popup just for this case. That is a lot of code for a rare failure.

I recommend (a).

Nothing is built yet. The work would happen in a new worktree, `.claude/worktrees/add-printer-popup` on branch `claude/add-printer-popup`, which I cut from jusprin-newui at `1cbce387d8`. None of this needs a live AI model call.
